findings.claim: One fresh-then-experienced player solves both in3 combinations, following the same5→7→10 construction template.
findings.counterevidence: Relative geometry differs and decomposition is still a real spatial inference. Fast formal AI performance does not establish human triviality.
findings.decision: Do not expand these same target-family levels. Retain as a small composition baseline.

findings.claim: Initial factorization gives an actual inference. Echo relocation reuses identical intermediate truth patterns; stricter support needs a small adaptation.
findings.counterevidence: Brute saturation is157–158 actions versus7 deliberate actions, so eventual closure is not a short winning shortcut. A fixed expression cannot satisfy conflicting contexts.
findings.decision: Test a structurally different relation, rather than more echo placements or more variables.

findings.claim: Changed relations require3/3/4 combinations and are genuinely different, but an experienced player found each complete construction before acting. Goal prose supplied substantial decomposition hints.
findings.counterevidence: A short intended insight can be worthwhile. General DNF construction is an adaptive method, not a single context-blind answer; no extra resources were added.
findings.decision: Do not expand this as a sequence of worksheets. Separate explicit case constraints from supplied target decompositions, and test useful persistence.

findings.claim: A fresh player completes three public-case stages in6 combinations, reusing the entire first-stage judgment as a later ingredient. It reports that reuse as the strongest moment.
findings.counterevidence: Player reports one preview; preview calls were not instrumented in these original runs. No mistakes or recovery; most construction is routine after recognizing minimal accepted pairs. Source expertise and observation conditions differ from the earlier experienced run.
findings.decision: Retain reusable constructed relationships as a logical hypothesis. This is one short puzzle sequence, not sustained fun or a completed civilization game.

findings.counterevidence: Choosing the distinguishing observation is real inference; joint condition is useful in4/12 worlds. No fresh agent run for this candidate.
findings.decision: Do not promote to a full game or add query credits to rescue it.

methodology.blindness: Instruction-based CLI restriction; fresh/experienced conditions recorded. No source or multi-step search allowed for agent players.
methodology.predictionCoding: Only explicitly structured expectedStatus fields are automatically scored. Other predictions remain recorded but unscored; confidence and eloquence earn no credit.
methodology.limits: One model/player per candidate family; prior formal expertise may make these puzzles unusually easy. No claim of human enjoyment or validated fun prediction.
methodology.counterexampleRule: Short shared solutions can expose routine play. Generic exhaustive solvability alone cannot reject a finite construction puzzle.
